unit: Students can describe their daily study routines, discuss learning tools, and share advice on building good study habits while balancing school and family life.
objective: Identify and talk about items used for studying.

title: Warm up
subtitle: Preparing to study
question: What tools do you usually bring to class for different school subjects?
starters: For English class, I always bring my...
When I go to the library, I need a...

title: Useful Language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat it.
Read the definition and example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: A book used for studying a school subject.
words.example: I need to read my history textbook for class tomorrow.
words.check: Do you usually read a textbook for fun or for school?

words.definition: A book with blank pages used for writing notes.
words.example: She takes all her math notes in a blue notebook.
words.check: Do you use a pen or a keyboard to write in a notebook?

title: Useful Language (Part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat it.
Read the definition and example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: A book or app that tells you the meanings of words.
words.example: I use a dictionary to learn new English words.
words.check: Which tool gives you the meanings of words: a notebook or a dictionary?

words.definition: Looking for information on the internet.
words.example: Doing an online search helps me find quick answers for my homework.
words.check: Do you do an online search using the internet or a piece of paper?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to explain why you need different study tools.

linkers.use: Explain what you do with a tool.
Explain why a tool is useful.
Explain which tool you need for a specific subject.

model:
Tutor: So, what do you need for your English class?
Student: Well, I need a dictionary for English. This helps me to learn new words.
Tutor: Right. What about a notebook?
Student: I use this to write down my notes.

your_turn.teacher: Ask the student which tools they need for a science or math class.
your_turn.student: Answer using the new phrases and vocabulary words, such as 'textbook' or 'online search'.

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine we have English, math, and history classes today. What tools do we need for these subjects? You can choose from a textbook, a notebook, a dictionary, or an online search. Use the sentence frames below to share your ideas.

title: Real-world scenario
role_a: You are a new student. You are at the bookstore to buy school supplies, but you aren't sure exactly what you need.
role_b: You are an experienced student. You are helping the new student choose the right study tools.
problem: The new student doesn't know which study tools to buy for their classes.
mission: Tell the new student which tools to buy.
Use: I need a... for... / I use this to... / This helps me to...
start: Hi there! I'm a new student here. Could you help me out? I'm not really sure what I need to buy for my classes.

title: Wrap-Up
recap: Vocabulary: textbook, notebook, dictionary, online search
Language chunks: I use this to... / This helps me to... / I need a... for...
Skill: Identifying and talking about items used for studying.
final_task: Use one of today's phrases to answer the question: What do you use a dictionary for?
challenge: Look around your room. Find three items and practice explaining what you use them for in English.
